headline: The Democratic sweep turned the AI unwind into a rotation: desks buy hyperscalers that own capacity and sell semis, memory, neoclouds and AI power, while AMD/ANET beats fade and the MRVL-LITE spread widens.
market_read: Mail from 3-5 Nov is dominated by the midterms: Democrats took both chambers and Texas, and GS Econ (4 Nov) puts states covering ~45% of planned US data-center capacity at risk of short-term moratoria. Desks describe one rotation: GS's TMT trading desk (5 Nov) saw heavy buying of hyperscalers against supply in names that build or power data centers, UBS PB (5 Nov) had hedge funds buying hyperscalers and software and selling hardware and memory, and BofA Short Analytics (4 Nov) measured Electric Grid Enablers -7.7σ and AI Infrastructure -5.0σ. Positioning was already light: GS (3 Nov) has fundamental and systematic L/S both down more than 3% in October, BofA (4 Nov) says clients sold US equities for a 3rd week, and JPM Market Intel (4-5 Nov) thinks HF de-risking is likely behind us and stays Tactically Bullish. Desks disagree on whether this pulls the semis peak into 2027 (UBS) or is just a funding trade, and earnings did not help: AMD gave back a +9% after-hours move (GS, 4 Nov) and ANET's +38-40% FY27 guide is one of the few beats that held.

up.why: The midterm read-across turned into an 'own installed compute' trade: GS's TMT trading desk (5 Nov) saw heavy, broad buying of hyperscalers against selling in anything that builds or powers data centers, UBS PB (5 Nov) had hedge funds buying hyperscalers at +1.1 std, and Barclays' Rand (5 Nov) says AMZN led because it has the most third-party compute. GS's desk relay (5 Nov) frames scarcity as good for owners and 'potentially disastrous' for builders. Bloomberg X has no AMZN spike (not among the risers through 4 Nov); the HOT band is 60-<80 (score 64.2), where AMZN's own 5-session analog median is -1.1% and 10-session -2.9% on only n=7, so the crowd is already fairly engaged. For 1-5 days the rotation has momentum while semis are the funding source; over 2-4 weeks the narrative needs the 'existing capacity reprices' idea to show up in pricing commentary, not just flows.
up.confirm: Hyperscaler outperformance vs SOX persists after the first oversold semis bounce; AWS pricing or capacity-scarcity comments in conferences.
up.weaken: Semis rebound sharply with hyperscalers lagging (the move was a funding trade), or Texas/Georgia moratorium talk fades as GS Econ expects.

up.why: The cleanest AI beat of the week: FY27 guided to +38-40% (MS, 3 Nov) against a ~33% bar at JPM (3 Nov) and ~35% at MS, though Barclays (3 Nov) heard high-40s buyside numbers, so the bar is disputed. Bernstein (4 Nov) notes estimates rise without a re-rating. Bloomberg X attention is up (z 1.40, Δz +1.78, tone +0.22, Δtone +0.16 through 4 Nov); the HOT band is 40-<60 (score 40.9) where ANET's own 5-session analog median is -0.7% (n=23) but the 10-session median is +2.5%. For 1-5 days it trades with the semis/AI-infra selloff (it rose up to 18% after hours, +6.5% next morning per GS); over 2-4 weeks it is one of the few AI-infra names where numbers move up and positioning is not crowded.
up.confirm: Holds most of the post-print gain while SOX keeps falling; estimate revisions follow through in the next week.
up.weaken: Gives back the gap as the data-center moratorium debate hits networking, or buyside high-40s FY27 numbers become the new bar.

up.why: Not a mail focus, but desk flow quietly leans long: SIG (3 Nov) saw 35k NVDA Mar 250/295 call spreads plus ~$300mn of 2027 QQQ calls, UBS's cash desk (5 Nov) saw buying in NVDA while selling AMD and INTC, BofA sales (3 Nov) put Long NVDA in its November US 10, and BofA's Franco (5 Nov) notes NVDA has de-rated >75% vs WMT on forward P/E. NVDA is not among Bloomberg X risers or fallers and has no analog row today. For 1-5 days NVDA is still inside the semis funding trade; over 2-4 weeks the case is that positioning has been cleared (GS PB October losses; JPM 'HF de-risking likely behind us').
up.confirm: NVDA outperforms SOX on down days; call-spread buying continues into the late-November print.
up.weaken: Data-center moratorium headlines spread beyond Texas/Georgia or hyperscaler capex commentary turns to deferral.

up.why: Sentiment was poor into the print (JPM survey -1 on 4 Nov; Barclays notes the stock down 42%), then COHR added a ~$20bn five-year PhotonLink NPO/CPO LTA, a 45% long-term GM target and a >60% FY27 growth guide vs Street ~50% (JPM, Barclays, MS, 4 Nov). But Jefferies (5 Nov) notes it did not hold the after-hours gains as AI hardware kept selling. Not in the Bloomberg X movers or analogs today. For 1-5 days it trades with the tape; over 2-4 weeks it is the optical name where expectations are low and visibility rose, with the MRVL-LITE deal keeping optics in focus.
up.confirm: Stock holds above the pre-print level as LITE reports (5 Nov AMC) and the optical expert calls (BofA LightCounting 5 Nov) land constructively.
up.weaken: LITE's print or the deal spread pulls optics lower again; investors treat the LTA as already-known demand.

down.why: The deal keeps getting worse in the mail: UBS special sits (4 Nov) says MRVL's fall turned a 24% premium for LITE into an 8-22% discount, UBS (3 Nov) has the spread at 12.7% with a 58% breakeven probability vs 76% for China-approval precedents, while Bernstein (3 Nov) says ~76% close odds are still too high; BofA (3 Nov) has downgraded to Neutral. DAMNANG (3 Nov, independent) is the contrarian voice arguing NVIDIA set the deal up. Bloomberg X: attention z 1.76, Δz +2.84 with flat tone (-0.02) and -37% over 7 sessions through 4 Nov; HOT band 40-<60 (53.7) where MRVL's own 5-session median is -0.8% and 10-session -1.8% (n=29). For 1-5 days the spread and the shareholder-vote debate dominate; over 2-4 weeks this stays weak unless terms change.
down.confirm: Spread widens further, or large MRVL holders signal a 'no' vote; China SAMR timing pushed out.
down.weaken: Revised terms (cash component, collar) or strong LITE results (5 Nov) re-anchor the value of the stock offer.

down.why: Neoclouds are the clearest midterm losers in the mail: GS TMT (4 Nov) 'hyperscalers higher vs neoclouds lower', Jefferies (4 Nov) CRWV -9.4% pre-market, UBS (5 Nov) Neoclouds -8.4% and CRWV among the cash-desk sells. UBS PB says hedge funds were not the main sellers, so this is long-only or retail supply. Not in today's Bloomberg X movers; HOT 39.9 and BULL 40.2, where CRWV's own BULL-band 5-session median is -8.6% (n=16). For 1-5 days pressure follows Texas news (bill prefiling 9 Nov per BofA); over 2-4 weeks financing costs (UBS: IG AI funding spread highest vs market since 2003) are the second leg.
down.confirm: Further Texas/Georgia moratorium headlines; wider neocloud bond or CDS levels.
down.weaken: GS Econ's view that moratoria are short-lived gains traction; new hyperscaler capacity contracts for neoclouds.

down.why: Memory is the funding source, not a broken thesis: UBS's cash desk (4 Nov) was a better seller of memory, UBS PB had hedge funds selling hardware and memory, and Jefferies' Asia desk (5 Nov) had Hynix -9.5%, Samsung -7.6%, Kioxia -13% as KOSPI fell ~5%. JPM's Asia research (4 Nov) stays firmly Overweight, and SIG (3 Nov) saw MU recovery call spreads, so the views diverge. Bloomberg X attention is falling (z 0.03, Δz -1.54) but tone is rising (+0.16, Δtone +0.19), a crowd leaving while the remaining voices get warmer. No analog row today. For 1-5 days it follows SOX and KOSPI; over 2-4 weeks the pricing data (TrendForce call 9 Nov, Nanya 10 Nov per BofA) decide whether this is unwinding or a buy.
down.confirm: Memory keeps underperforming on days semis bounce; foreign selling in KOSPI continues.
down.weaken: DRAM contract prices or LTAs printed strong in the November checks; memory leads the first semis rebound.

down.why: NOW is the most-discussed name with negative tone on Bloomberg X (z 2.21, Δz +2.16, tone -0.18, Δtone -0.23, -27.5% over 7 sessions through 4 Nov). The HOT band is 80-100 (83.4), where NOW's own 5-session median is -1.1% on only n=4. Desks: GS's Callahan (3 Nov) says inference-economy software only works if growth accelerates, and UBS's cash desk (5 Nov) had NOW among the sells even as software was bought. For 1-5 days the 'software as a refuge' rotation is not lifting NOW; over 2-4 weeks it needs evidence that AI is adding to growth, not cannibalising it.
down.confirm: NOW keeps lagging IGV while software is bought; tone stays negative on Bloomberg X.
down.weaken: Software rotation broadens to NOW; peers (TEAM, NET, OKTA) print acceleration.

down.why: AI power took the cleanest policy hit: the Democratic sweep and the Texas governor result raise data-center moratorium risk (GS Econ: states covering ~45% of planned US capacity; Texas ~25%). GS Research (relayed 5 Nov) flags negative reactions for VST, NRG, CEG and others; BofA Short Analytics (4 Nov) measured Electric Grid Enablers -7.7σ, and UBS's energy specialist had AI Industrials -635bp vs SOXX, the widest one-day spread in 3+ years. VST is not in today's Bloomberg X movers or analogs. For 1-5 days, Texas bill prefiling (9 Nov) keeps the risk live; over 2-4 weeks GS expects the issue to fade.
down.confirm: Texas prefiled bills include moratorium or tax-break repeal language; IPP drawdowns extend.
down.weaken: Hinojosa's team signals grid-investment priorities over moratoria; IPPs bounce with lower rates.

themes.title: Compute owners vs compute builders (desks agree on the trade, disagree on why)
themes.text: Every desk we read after the Democratic sweep describes the same rotation: hyperscalers bought, and semis, memory, neoclouds and AI power sold as the funding source (GS trading 5 Nov, UBS PB 5 Nov, Jefferies 5 Nov, BofA Egan 4 Nov). The disagreement is about mechanism. GS's desk relay and UBS's Dwyer argue that scarce energised capacity becomes more valuable and capex falls, so FCF improves. Barclays' Rand says it is about capacity owned today, not a capex cut. UBS frames the semis debate as whether the 2028/29 peak is pulled into 2027 or the cycle is stretched. JPM Market Intel stays Tactically Bullish and says HF de-risking is likely behind us; UBS PB found hedge-fund flows muted in the selloff, so the supply came from elsewhere.

themes.title: MRVL-LITE: the arb market and the independents read it differently
themes.text: UBS special sits (3-4 Nov) shows a 12.7% spread and 58% breakeven probability, far wider than China-approval precedents, and the offer is now at a discount for LITE holders. Bernstein's analyst, relayed 3 Nov, still thinks ~76% close odds are too high. DAMNANG (independent author, 3 Nov, preview only) argues the opposite reading, that NVIDIA arranged the deal and the 'optics war' is starting. LITE reports 5 Nov after the close, and BofA's LightCounting expert call (5 Nov) covers the deal.

themes.title: SemiAnalysis on SpaceX 13GW vs the election tape
themes.text: SemiAnalysis (3 Nov) says SpaceX lifted its 2027 datacenter target to ~13GW with >9GW identified and 3.6GW under construction (their GW basis, not reconciled to the wiki's facility/IT-load bases). A day later SPCX was among the biggest election losers (Jefferies Titu and pre-market screen, 4 Nov; JPM 4 Nov). The build-speed bull case and the moratorium risk now point in opposite directions for the same name.

themes.title: DAMNANG on substrates, and the same names in the Asia selloff
themes.text: DAMNANG (4 Nov, independent author) argues the substrate shortage lasts until 2031 and that larger substrates yield fewer good units. On 5 Nov Jefferies' Asia desk had Ibiden -16%, all the Taiwanese ABF names -10% and MLCCs -10-17%, so the bottleneck names were sold as AI hardware. That is a sentiment and positioning move, not a fundamental change in the article's thesis.

coverage_gaps: The window spans two days (3 Nov 11:15Z to 5 Nov 13:02Z) because no review was written on 4 Nov; 3 Nov morning items already in the 3 Nov review (AAPL, MRVL-LITE first reactions) were not re-recorded.

Bodies are capped at ~12,000 characters by the collector, and we read the first ~2,500 of each: later sections (UBS PB detail, JPM Chips for Breakfast surveys for MCHP and others, BofA Idea Bank, Jefferies 'AI Positioning Thoughts' and data-center update of 5 Nov) were not read.

DAMNANG (3 Nov MRVL-LITE, 4 Nov substrates) and SemiAnalysis (3 Nov SpaceX) arrived as previews only; paywalled sections not read. The substrates piece names no universe ticker in the preview and is a theme note only.
Bernstein, IREN/CIFR (Bernstein TX data-center TP cuts), HUBS, Ibiden and FN drew desk comment but are outside the universe and were not recorded as observations.
LITE reports 5 Nov after the close; MCHP, NET, DKNG and AAOI also report tonight, after this window.
source_notes: Channel: Outlook desktop via COM (desk_mail_collect.ps1), 1842 messages screened across 19 folders, 615 bodies retrieved, inbox lag 0 h, newest received 2026-11-05T13:01:51Z.
